acceptance_criteria.text: lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex derives PLATFORM_ADMIN via Letflow.Api.Authorization.roles_from_strings/1, so exactly one code path maps role strings to the PLATFORM_ADMIN role
acceptance_criteria.evidence: §2 shows the @spec and before/after derivation comments for check_tenant_status/2. §5 pseudocode shows Authorization.roles_from_strings(raw_roles) called before the cond guard. §7 cross-module dependency table names the full @spec roles_from_strings([String.t()]) :: [role()] and its location in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex. The atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN is compared against the [role()] list, making roles_from_strings/1 structurally required.

acceptance_criteria.text: the tenant-inactive-403 exemption behavior for PLATFORM_ADMIN is unchanged, proven by a test exercising both an exempt PLATFORM_ADMIN and a non-exempt actor against an inactive tenant
acceptance_criteria.evidence: §5 pseudocode shows the cond semantics are identical to pre-fix (only the roles derivation line changes). §6.1 test table specifies: (row 1) call_plug(:get, tenant.id, ["PLATFORM_ADMIN"]) → refute conn.halted (exempt); (row 2) call_plug(:get, tenant.id, ["PROCESS_OPERATOR"]) → conn.status == 403 (non-exempt). Both test cases target the inactive-tenant path. Test file location is named: test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs, describe block 'ISS-0808 — PLATFORM_ADMIN check uses Authorization.roles_from_strings/1'.

acceptance_criteria.text: a regression test would fail if the plug reverted to the raw string comparison
acceptance_criteria.evidence: §4 (Atom-vs-String Design: Structural Regression Guard) gives a complete failure-mode walkthrough: atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN can never be a member of a [String.t()] list, so removing roles_from_strings/1 while keeping the atom constant means the exemption never fires → 403 always returned → 'refute conn.halted' in AC2 test fails. §6.1 table row 1 names the specific test and failure mode explicitly.
